stem: A root-zone sample has elevated EC, but roots appear healthy, irrigation delivery is uneven, and symptoms are concentrated in one zone. Which approach best supports a defensible differential?
choices: Interpret EC together with moisture, drainage, irrigation delivery, pH, root condition, crop pattern, and recent history rather than treating EC as a single-cause diagnosis.
Declare nutrient toxicity because elevated EC always proves excessive nutrient uptake.
Ignore irrigation uniformity because EC already identifies the cause.
Average all zones together so the local pattern does not affect the conclusion.
rationale: Root-zone measurements are interacting evidence. EC must be interpreted with water status, delivery, pH, roots, spatial pattern, and management history.
